_about: Help text shown under each decision, and the words on choice buttons. Keys match packages/operating-model/data/levers.csv.

gas_stations.title: Gas stations
gas_stations.intro: Most Cordell stations are owned by local dealers. You set what Cordell charges them for fuel, in cents a gallon above or below the going rate in their area. The dealers then decide what to charge drivers. In Europe, Halden owns its stations and sets the pump price itself.

help.rigs: How many rigs drill new wells in Texas next quarter. A new well takes about three months to start pumping, and every rig costs $40 million a quarter whether its wells pay off or not.
help.norway: Keep pumping as planned, or pump less. Pumping less saves the cost of getting those barrels out. Keep in mind Norway takes 78% in tax, which cuts both ways.
help.br_run: As a share of everything the refinery can handle. Above 97%, the plant wears out faster.
help.rot_posture: Keep it running, pause it, or close it. Pausing saves the costs that come with each barrel, but you still pay the fixed costs like staff and upkeep. Restarting after a pause costs about $85 million. Closing is for good.
help.rot_run: As a share of everything Rotterdam can handle.
help.sg_request: This is a request, not an order. Straits Pacific owns 60% of the refinery and makes the call. You'll hear their answer with your results.
help.tp: The price per barrel Baton Rouge pays Halden's own oil fields. It moves profit between the oil fields, the refinery and Geneva. It doesn't change Halden's total profit.

tp_method.cost: What it costs to pump and ship

station_notes.off_urban: Lots of stations nearby; drivers switch for a few cents
station_notes.off_de: Drivers cross the border for cheaper fuel

oil_fields.title: Norway fields partners run
oil_fields.text: Halden owns part of these and pays its share of the bills, but the partners decide how much to pump. Right now they're pumping as planned.

oil_fields.title: Kessana, offshore West Africa
oil_fields.text: Runs under Halden's contract with the Kessana government. You don't set this one.
